topics: Arrangements with identical items or restrictions

items.title: Permutations
items.body: Ordered arrangements: \(^nP_r=\dfrac{n!}{(n-r)!}\). Order matters. \(n\) objects in a line: \(n!\) ways.

items.title: Combinations
items.body: Unordered selections: \(^nC_r=\dbinom{n}{r}=\dfrac{n!}{r!(n-r)!}\). Order does not matter.

items.title: Restrictions
items.body: Always together: treat as one unit, then \((n-1)!\times r!\). Never together: total − (always together).

items.title: Circular Arrangements
items.body: \((n-1)!\) ways to arrange \(n\) objects in a circle (one position is fixed).

body.en: Permutation (order matters): \(^nP_r=\dfrac{n!}{(n-r)!}\). Combination (order does not matter): \(^nC_r=\dbinom{n}{r}=\dfrac{n!}{r!\,(n-r)!}\). Arrangements with identical items: divide by the factorial of each repeated item. With restrictions: fix the restricted items first, then arrange the rest.

caption.en: Combinations \(\binom{6}{r}\) for \(r = 0, 1, \ldots, 6\), displaying the symmetric binomial coefficient distribution peaking at \(r = 3\).

body.en:
Permutation vs Combination: If order or role matters (e.g. President and Vice President, line order, distinct positions), use permutations \(^nP_r\). If order does not matter (e.g. selecting a committee of 3 students), use combinations \(^nC_r\).

Identical items vs Distinct slots: Arranging \(n\) objects where some are identical requires dividing by each repeat count: \(\frac{n!}{p!\,q!\cdots}\).

'Together' vs 'Separated': For items that must stay together, glue them as a single super-element and arrange \((n - k + 1)!\), then multiply by \(k!\) for internal order. For items that must NEVER be adjacent, arrange the unrestricted items first, creating slots \(\underline{\quad}\star\underline{\quad}\star\dots\), and choose slot positions.

A committee of 4 is chosen from 5 men and 6 women. Find the number of ways if the committee must contain at least 2 women.

Exactly 2W: \(\binom{6}{2}\binom{5}{2}=15\times10=150\). Exactly 3W: \(\binom{6}{3}\binom{5}{1}=20\times5=100\). Exactly 4W: \(\binom{6}{4}\binom{5}{0}=15\). Total: \(265\).

How many different arrangements are there of the letters of the word BANANA?

6 letters; N appears 2 times, A appears 3 times: \(\dfrac{6!}{3!\,2!}=\dfrac{720}{12}=60\).

question.en: In how many ways can 5 people be seated in a row if two particular people (A and B) must not sit next to each other?

solution.en: Total \(=5!=120\). Cases where A & B are adjacent: treat AB as a block → \(4!\times2=48\). Answer: \(120-48=72\).

question.en: Find the number of ways to arrange the 7 letters in the word SUCCESS.

solution.en: The word SUCCESS has 7 letters with 3 S's, 2 C's, 1 U, and 1 E. The number of distinct permutations is \(\frac{7!}{3!\,2!} = \frac{5040}{6 \times 2} = \frac{5040}{12} = 420\).
